argument:
TSMC's 36% revenue growth and operating-margin expansion to 60.3% demonstrate substantial recurring foundry improvement. H1 CFO exceeded capex by NT$635.576bn, and cash/marketables exceeded interest-bearing debt by NT$2,486.33bn. These observations support internally funded capacity growth and provide financial resilience for a buy thesis at estimated 22x forward earnings.

NT$63.20bn Vanguard disposal/mark gains enhance net-income growth, so operating metrics are the cleaner anchor. Inventory days rose to 87, guided operating margin falls to 56–58%, and Taiwan geopolitics cannot be neutralised by cash. Nevertheless, measured post-capex cash and strong operating profitability make expansion financing manageable. The high trailing multiple still needs continuing execution, while RSI near 88 discourages chasing. Purchase logic is participation in profitable foundry demand, not assuming peak margins or guidance are guaranteed.
key_points: Operating growth and margin expansion support recurring economics.
Net liquidity and positive post-capex cash fund investment internally.
Geopolitics, inventory and lower guided margins constrain premium valuation.
